chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about one who took land without its right and built upon it. He said: 'He removes his building and hands over the soil to its owner, for there is no right for the root of a tyrant.'
Then he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever takes land without its right is obliged to carry its soil to the Place of Gathering (Resurrection).'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a building constructed on usurped land?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling of *ghasb* (usurpation), establishing that the builder does not automatically acquire ownership of the land through construction. It highlights the principle that the oppressor bears the physical burden of their transgression, a concept reinforced by the Prophet’s statement that the usurper will carry the soil on the Day of Resurrection, linking legal restitution to eschatological accountability.
